title: Non-Aligned Atomic Access (Bus Lock Overhead)
pattern: Declaring an atomic variable inside a packed struct such that it straddles a cache-line boundary.
why_bad: Performing an atomic operation on an unaligned variable that straddles two cache lines requires a hardware "bus lock" or complex split-lock sequence. This stalls the memory bus, slowing down every CPU core in the system by orders of magnitude.
detection: Atomic types located inside byte-aligned or packed structures where their offset is not a multiple of their size.
counterexample: Ensuring all atomic variables are strictly aligned to their natural size boundaries.
